title: Weighted averages of arithmetic functions and applications to equidistribution and ergodic theory
summary: For a wide range of functions $W\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, we establish a general result for estimating weighted averages of the form\[\mathbb{E}^{W}_{n \le N} f(\vartheta(n))= \frac{1}{W(N)}\sum_{n=1}^N (W(n)-W(n-1))f(\vartheta(n)),\]where $f\colon \{1,\ldots,N\}\to\mathbb{C}$ is an arbitrary function, and $\vartheta(n)$ is any arithmetic function that adheres to a certain Gaussian distribution condition. (For instance, one may take $\vartheta(n)=Ω(n)$, where $Ω(n)$ counts the number of prime factors of $n$ with multiplicity, or $\vartheta(n)=s_q(p_n)$, where $s_q$ is the sum-of-digits…
